abstract: The axon initial segment (AIS) is fundamental to action potential initiation, neuronal polarity maintenance, and plasticity. Despite its functional importance, AIS remains understudied partially due to the lack of molecular tools with high subcellular specificity. By engineering an ultra-high affinity (Kd ~0.37 nM) small binder (16 kDa) that exclusively targets 480-kDa ankyrin-G, the master scaffold of AIS, and integrating neuronal type-specific promoters with feedback-regulated expression elements, we developed an efficient, portable method for delivering tightly controlled amounts of proteins or organelles to the AIS with unprecedented specificity, enabling selective, tunable, and near-endogenous-level AIS targeting in defined neuronal populations both in vitro and in vivo. Coupled with a toolkit of AIS modulators that we characterized, this strategy achieves directed manipulation of AIS structure, real-time monitoring of AIS plasticity dynamics and fast degradation of the entire AIS compartment, in desired neuronal types. Thus, our method provides new opportunities for dissecting AIS physiology and pathology, facilitating the development of therapeutics for AIS-linked brain disorders.
